text:
maya: Need a final decision on webinar topic by EOD. Options: 1) Practical inference economics, 2) Deploying inference reliably, 3) Benchmarking real-world prompts. Thoughts?
aj: Leaning into "Practical inference economics"  gives us direct hooks to cost/playbooks. Could pair with a short benchmark slide.
rachel: Agree on economics. For abstracts: short (50-70 words) + 2 bullet takeaways. I'll draft 2 variants.
maya: Cool. Speakers: AJ (runtime), Tony (customers & cost ops), me as host. Tony, can you do case anecdotes?
tonY: I can, but short anecdotes only (1-2 mins each). Will prepare metrics and one slide.
aj: Rehearsal plan: T-60 panel join, T-25 slides review, T-10 mic check, 0 go live. Can we do a 20-min tech dry-run Tues?
rachel: I can coordinate. I'll create a rehearsal invite and add run-of-show in the doc. opsbot can you create calendar slot?
opsbot: calendar-invite: created for 2026-05-12T10:00:00Z (participants: maya, aj, rachel, tony). reminder=30m :white_check_mark:
maya: Run-of-show draft: 0-5 welcome, 5-20 thesis & benchmarks, 20-35 demo + cost breakdown, 35-50 panel Q&A, 50-60 closing CTA. Use slide numbers for cueing.
aj: For benchmark slide include methodology note: "real prompt mix, mixed batch, p90 latency". Keep headline simple: "~3x cost improvement in our tests"
rachel: I'll draft two abstracts and two one-liners for socials. Want A/B headlines: cost-first vs reliability-first?
maya: We go cost-first. Rachel, deliver by EOD so we can lock speaker brief. Also add a consent checkbox for clips in the speaker prep doc.
tony: Will rehearse anecdotes and upload 2 sample slides to the shared deck.
maya: Thanks — final: AJ owns demo slides, Tony owns customer slides, Rachel owns abstracts + social copy, Maya owns run-of-show + host cues. Post updates here.
